name: MemoryOS
ontology_notes: Hierarchical OS metaphor. Short-term QA pairs, mid-term consolidated segments, long-term user profile string plus user knowledge deque and assistant knowledge deque (LongTermMemory in memoryos-pypi/long_term.py). No typed relationship state, lore, or OOC. Profile is a merged text blob per user_id.

ontology.evidence: README: short-term, mid-term, long-term persona memory. long_term.py LongTermMemory holds user_profiles[user_id], knowledge_base (user), assistant_knowledge. Those are strings and deques, not companion tables.
ontology.label: measured

write_policy.evidence: memoryos.py add_memory stores user_input and agent_response as a QA pair in short-term. Updater evicts to mid-term when STM is full, then LLM-extracts profile insights and knowledge. The model decides long-term text. No write refusal.
write_policy.label: measured

read_policy.evidence: README Retrieval: Retriever fetches short-term history, mid-term segments, user profile and knowledge, and assistant knowledge for Generation. Always retrieve-then-prompt. Empty knowledge deques yield no long-term hits.
read_policy.label: measured

supersession.evidence: long_term.py update_user_profile(merge=True) concatenates new text under an Updated on timestamp header rather than replacing a field. merge=False overwrites. Knowledge deques drop oldest at capacity. No invalidate-with-time.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Entries carry timestamp via get_timestamp(). Mid-term and long-term are capacity queues, not validity windows. LoCoMo numbers include temporal questions but the store does not expose last-Tuesday queries.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: user_id keys the profile. User knowledge and assistant knowledge are separate deques. Relationship state would land in the user profile string. No character vs relationship type.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Retriever is embedding/keyword over the four stores. No skip of a relevant hit for social reasons.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: QA pairs and extracted profile text are stored as-is. No provenance, trust tags, or jailbreak filter in long_term.py or README.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: Capacity eviction on knowledge deques (knowledge_capacity). STM flush to mid-term. No documented user forget-that API. MCP tools listed in README are add and get_user_profile, not delete.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Each add may embed the QA. Updater calls an LLM when STM is full. Retrieval embeds the query and pulls top segments plus the whole profile string into Generation, which is another LLM call. Cost grows with mid-term size until capacity caps it.
cost_shape.label: inferred

local.evidence: Apache-2.0. memoryos-pypi and memoryos-chromadb run on one machine with local files/FAISS/Chroma. LLM and embedding model are caller-supplied (OpenAI or local names in README).
local.label: measured

mcp.evidence: Official memoryos-mcp/ in the same repo. README MemoryOS-MCP Getting Started: tools include add_memory and get_user_profile with user_id in mcp.json.
mcp.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: It is a personalization OS with a user profile and a separate assistant knowledge base, which is closer to companion than plain Graph-RAG. Profile is an appended string, relationship is not a type, forgetting is capacity not user erase, and there is no silence. Generation is retrieve-then-prompt.

published_eval.name: LoCoMo
published_eval.claimed_score: Average improvements of 49.11% F1 and 46.18% BLEU-1 on LoCoMo (README). Relative to their baseline, not an absolute accuracy.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: LoCoMo fact QA F1/BLEU-1 on long conversations. Not character drift, social silence, or poisoning.

open_unknowns: Absolute LoCoMo F1 for MemoryOS vs the unnamed baseline in the 49.11% relative claim.
Whether MCP exposes delete or only add/get_user_profile in the current memoryos-mcp tree.
Paper PDF internals beyond the README (Paper-MemoryOS.pdf in repo).
